defs.def: a weapon that is sent through the air and that explodes when it hits the thing that it is aimed at 导弹

ex.s: In the 1960s and 1970s, the greatest fear was that the human race, and possibly all advanced life forms on the planet, could be wiped out by nuclear missiles, just at the push of a button.
ex.t: 在1960年代和1970年代，最大的恐惧是人类，甚至可能是地球上所有的先进生命形式，都会被核导弹只需按一下按钮就彻底消灭。

ex.s: He played a key role in China’s missile and aviation programmes, helping fast-track the development by decades.
ex.t: 他在中国的导弹和航空项目中发挥了关键作用，帮助将发展进程加快了数十年。

ex.s: He received a hero’s welcome from his homeland and was put in charge of not only developing China’s rocket science but also its space and missile programme.
ex.t: 他受到了来自祖国的英雄般的欢迎，不仅负责开发中国的火箭科学，还负责其太空和导弹计划。

ex.s: When he was asked “Can we Chinese possibly make missiles?”, his reply was a determined “Why not?
ex.t: 当有人问他＂我们中国人能造出导弹吗？＂时，他的回答是坚定的＂为什么不能？

ex.s: We Chinese are able to make the same things that other people make.” Under Qian’s leadership, China developed the Dongfeng missiles, followed by the first generation of Long March rockets.
ex.t: 我们中国人能够做出别人能做的东西。在钱学森的领导下，中国开发了东风导弹，随后是第一代长征火箭。

defs.def: an object that is thrown at sb to hurt them 发射物；投掷物
